memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe and put the ephod on him. He also fastened the ephod with a decorated waistband, which he tied around him." - Lev 8:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Every verb in this verse has Moses as its subject. He put. He tied. He clothed. He fastened.

Aaron stands still and is dressed.

There is a grown man being clothed like a child, in front of the entire nation. It cannot have been comfortable for his dignity. But it made something unmistakably clear: the high priest did not provide his own qualifications for standing before God.

Scripture returns to this image again and again. Adam and Eve sewed fig leaves; God made garments of skin and clothed them (Gen 3:21). The prodigal son came home rehearsing a speech and his father called for the best robe (Lk 15:22). Zechariah saw Joshua the high priest in filthy clothes, and the angel said, See, I have taken away your sin, and I will put fine garments on you (Zech 3:4).

And Isaiah rejoiced: He has clothed me with garments of salvation and arrayed me in a robe of his righteousness (Isa 61:10).

You do not weave your own righteousness. It is put on you.

That is worth remembering on the days when you feel least presentable. What you wear before God was never your own tailoring.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What am I trusting in to make me presentable before God?
2. Can I receive Christ's righteousness as a gift rather than an achievement?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You clothe me in a righteousness I could never make. Help me to wear it with gratitude today. Amen.
